benchmarks.name: WebGameBench — Usable rate
benchmarks.description: WebGameBench (arXiv 2605.17637, Baidu): 111 frozen Structured WebGame Specifications (7 gameplay families, D1-D4 difficulty) that a coding agent must turn into a deployed browser-native game; a Codex CLI (gpt-5.4 xhigh) runtime evaluator plays the game in Chrome via Playwright and assigns EXCELLENT/USABLE/UNUSABLE. Usable rate = share of valid scored samples labeled EXCELLENT or USABLE. Evaluator agrees with human gameplay review at 85.0% accuracy (XHigh) on the Usable criterion. Higher is better.

benchmarks.name: WebGameBench — Excellent rate
benchmarks.description: WebGameBench (arXiv 2605.17637): same 111 browser-native game tasks; Excellent rate = share of valid scored samples whose delivered game fully and stably satisfies the specification (label EXCELLENT). Stricter signal; exact three-way label agreement with humans only 50%. Higher is better.

benchmarks.name: TeleSWEBench — Stage 1 Exact-Match localization (cumulative)
benchmarks.description: TeleSWEBench (arXiv 2606.05001, NCSU/UCSD): 734 commit-derived tasks (Easy 142 / Medium 279 / Difficult 313) mined from the srsRAN 5G C++ repository, each with executable unit tests. Stage 1 metric: share of tasks where the agent modified exactly the ground-truth file set (P = T), cumulative over all tiers; AIDER CLI harness with 300 s cutoff (timeouts excluded). Higher is better.

benchmarks.description: TeleSWEBench (arXiv 2606.05001, NCSU/UCSD): 734 commit-derived tasks (Easy 142 / Medium 279 / Difficult 313) mined from the srsRAN 5G C++ repository, each with executable unit tests. benchmarks.name: TeleSWEBench — TeleJudge Acceptance Rate (TAR)
benchmarks.description: TeleSWEBench (arXiv 2606.05001, NCSU/UCSD): 734 commit-derived tasks (Easy 142 / Medium 279 / Difficult 313) mined from the srsRAN 5G C++ repository, each with executable unit tests. benchmarks.name: TeleSWEBench — Ship-Ready Percentage (SRP)

benchmarks.name: CoDA-Bench — Execution Accuracy (Codex CLI scaffold)
benchmarks.description: CoDA-Bench (arXiv 2606.15300, Renmin Univ., ICML 2026): 1,009 data-intensive analytical tasks over a Kaggle-derived Linux sandbox (31 data communities, ~980 files per environment, SNR 0.0105); agent must discover the relevant files and write code to produce the answer. CoDA-Hard = 119-task subset needing >=2 target files and >30-line reference solutions. DA = Discovery Accuracy (correct target files located); EA = Execution Accuracy (task output correct). Higher is better. Scaffold: Codex CLI (official default configuration for native CLI tools; unified framework for OpenHands / Mini-SWE-agent).

CoDA-Hard = 119-task subset needing >=2 target files and >30-line reference solutions. DA = Discovery Accuracy (correct target files located); EA = Execution Accuracy (task output correct). Higher is better. Scaffold: Claude Code (official default configuration for native CLI tools; unified framework for OpenHands / Mini-SWE-agent).

benchmarks.name: TUA-Bench — success rate (Claude Code scaffold)
benchmarks.description: TUA-Bench (arXiv 2606.28480, Meta AI): 120 manually designed general-purpose terminal-use tasks in 5 families (Office & Productivity, Web & Information, System & Software Ops, Scientific & Engineering, Multimedia & Design), each with deterministic setup script and execution-based verifier; GUI-type tasks reformulated as terminal tasks. Success rate = per-task pass rate averaged over 5 independent runs; 2400 s per-task limit. Best: Claude Code + Opus 4.8 (max) 65.8%. Higher is better. Scaffold: Claude Code.

benchmarks.name: SWE-Interact — single-turn baseline resolve rate

benchmarks.name: GameEngineBench — pass@1
benchmarks.description: GameEngineBench (arXiv 2607.03525, Nitrode / Nexon Intelligence Labs): 110 scoped C++ implementation tasks inside Unreal Engine 5 projects from 9 real game repositories (gameplay, multiplayer, AI, animation, UI, persistence, XR, rendering plugins); patch must compile and pass behavioral tests run via Unreal automation in PIE listen-server mode. One attempt per task, solver timeout 3600 s. Each model is run through its vendor's native CLI wrapper (codex, claude-code, Antigravity CLI, qwen-code, kimi-code), so harness effects are mixed in. 31 tasks unsolved by all configs. Higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Atrex-Bench — correctness pass rate
benchmarks.description: Atrex-Bench (arXiv 2607.14541, Alibaba ATREX): trace-driven GPU-kernel generation benchmark — 30 operators and 440 shapes sampled from production inference traces of compute-limited memory-rich XPU-A GPUs, each with an importance weight (share of GPU time) and a roofline ceiling; agents must write kernels in the FlyDSL target DSL (unfamiliar to pretraining corpora). Vanilla one-pass setting, same prompt/tools, Claude Code runtime (GPT-5.5 on Codex). Operator-balanced fraction of shapes passing correctness (fallbacks to PyTorch count). Higher is better.

benchmarks.name: SWE-NFI — functional preservation check pass rate (Codex CLI scaffold)
benchmarks.description: SWE-NFI (arXiv 2607.27409, York Univ. et al.): 188 non-functional-improvement tasks from real merged PRs in open-source Python projects; 5 NFI aspects (Documentation, Error Handling, Library Constraints, Coding Style, Logic Patterns) operationalized as 92 executable rules. Outputs must first pass task-specific functional preservation checks (FPC); NFI improvement = change in normalized rule score vs original code (percentage points), averaged over 5 runs. Human reference FPC 100%, aggregate improvement ~ Doc 8.0 / EH 2.0 / LC 1.1 / CS 1.5 / LP 1.5. Higher is better. Share of valid outputs passing all task-specific functional preservation checks. Scaffold: Codex CLI.

benchmarks.description: SWE-NFI (arXiv 2607.27409, York Univ. et al.): 188 non-functional-improvement tasks from real merged PRs in open-source Python projects; 5 NFI aspects (Documentation, Error Handling, Library Constraints, Coding Style, Logic Patterns) operationalized as 92 executable rules. Outputs must first pass task-specific functional preservation checks (FPC); NFI improvement = change in normalized rule score vs original code (percentage points), averaged over 5 runs. Human reference FPC 100%, aggregate improvement ~ Doc 8.0 / EH 2.0 / LC 1.1 / CS 1.5 / LP 1.5. Higher is better. Aggregate agent NFI improvement I_NFI(a) over valid outputs passing FPC (Table 5, average of 5 runs). Scaffold: Claude Code.

benchmarks.name: LoopsBench — Resolve Rate (Codex loop)
benchmarks.description: LoopsBench (arXiv 2608.00267, Microsoft / Nanjing Univ.): long-horizon loop-engineering benchmark — each task is a dependency DAG over separately testable development units recovered from authentic sources (8 programming languages, >5,300 development units); a dependency-aware runtime releases tests along the ready frontier and retains passed tests as regression obligations. Resolve Rate (RR) = tasks fully resolved; Test Pass Rate (TPR) = fraction of released tests passed; 'w/' = with outer continuation loop. Single trial per config. Higher is better. Loop implementation: Codex; 'w/' outer continuation setting.

benchmarks.name: VulnGym Hard — end-to-end Advisory Recall (Claude Code scaffold)

End-to-end task T1 on the Hard subset (trace length >= 9; 31 advisories / 46 entries): AR = Advisory Recall, ER = Entry Recall, ES = Edit Similarity of predicted trace. Higher is better. Scaffold: Claude Code.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified (200-task sample) — Vanilla re-run in SWE-Touch (mini-swe-agent)
benchmarks.description: SWE-Touch (arXiv 2608.02499, CASIA): stress-tests coding agents in a shared workspace via validated Counter-Edits — plausible user code edits that conflict with task completion, injected (with a short user message) when the agent reaches the task-critical region. Main cohort: seeded 200-task sample of SWE-bench Verified, Mini-SWE-Agent harness on Harbor, 100-step budget, mean of 3 runs. Longer-horizon extension: 25 SWE-Bench Pro + 25 DeepSWE tasks, 500-step budget, K=3 edits injected at 25/50/75% of the Vanilla trajectory, mean of 2 runs. Higher is better. Vanilla (no user edit) resolve rate on the 200-task Verified sample — re-run of other vendors' models by the SWE-Touch authors.

benchmarks.name: MT-Web2Code — Macro-Level regional reconstruction Score
benchmarks.description: MT-Web2Code (arXiv 2608.03474, HIT / Meituan): multimodal multi-turn web-UI coding benchmark for coding agents. Macro-Level Regional Reconstruction: rebuild a missing region of an existing page from a visual reference, scored by VLM rubric (Kimi-K2.6 judge; Layout/Element/Text/Color/Spacing + overall; Score = final composite). Micro-Level Localized Modification: fix a localized defect (9-type taxonomy), scored by pixel alignment (in-box repair S_inbox, out-of-box preservation S_outbox; Score = composite). Mean of 3 runs. Higher is better. Macro-Level composite Score.

benchmarks.name: GameXpert-Bench GameGen — Overall score
benchmarks.description: GameXpert-Bench (arXiv 2608.21833, Tencent Hunyuan / Lightspeed): three-track game-development lifecycle benchmark for coding agents. GameGen = 97 single-request browser-native game generation tasks (11 genres, 44 3D) built with Claude Code under default configuration, judged by an evidence-grounded LLM judge on Completeness / Richness / Player Experience / Visual Quality (Overall = mean, 0-100). GameFix = repair of 50 confidential Gold Games corrupted by reversible mutation operators; STRICT = mean height of the average@3 survival curve over all-solved threshold band tau in [90,100] (3 runs). GameOpt = human-guided multi-turn refinement over 17 JavaScript games / 102 requests, six-dimension discrimination-weighted score (0-100). Higher is better. GameGen Overall (Table 2), Claude Code default harness.

benchmarks.name: HVTB — reward-hack rate, Ablation prompt (no anti-hack instruction)
benchmarks.description: Hack-Verifiable Terminal Bench / HVTB (arXiv 2608.22103, Tel Aviv Univ. / UCSB): the 89 Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks instrumented with two planted, deterministically detectable reward hacks (a leaked hidden solution and readable held-out tests in an admin/ directory). Metric = any-hack rate: share of completed runs that triggered at least one planted hack. Prompt classes: Ablation = no hacking-related instruction; L0 = generic 'solve on your own / do not hack'; L1-L3 = progressively more specific disclosure of the vulnerability. Each model runs in its native harness (Claude Code, Codex, gemini-cli; terminus-2 for open models). Lower is better. Setting: Ablation prompt (no anti-hack instruction).

benchmarks.name: OpenHarmony Bench — Task Completion (all 153 tasks)
benchmarks.description: OpenHarmony Bench v1.0 (arXiv 2608.16022, Huawei / Beihang / Fudan): app-level coding benchmark on OpenHarmony ArkTS applications — 153 top-level tasks (32 new-feature, 50 spec-driven with 139 F-points, 71 bug-fix); the delivered project must build and the requested behavior is verified by driving the app on a device/emulator. Task Completion = final project builds AND all executable checks pass; mean over 3 full-suite runs. All configs use Huawei's DevEco Code agent (v0.1.0-1.3, temperature 0, 200K context, 65.5K reasoning budget, <=5 compile-repair iterations). Higher is better. Scope: all 153 tasks.

benchmarks.name: SWE Refactor Bench — score (out of 100)
benchmarks.description: SWE Refactor Bench (arXiv 2608.23564, Navers Lab / Einsia.AI / Tsinghua): 20 long-horizon whole-repository stack-migration tasks over 4 technical-debt classes (build toolchain, platform port, framework rewrite, language rewrite), one run per task per configuration (26 model-effort configs, 520 runs). Three-stage evaluation: (I) Migration Audit (LLM-judged migration criteria), (II) fixed Behavioural Tests, (III) Agentic Verification by 6 independent coding agents generating counterexample tests. GPT-series via Codex, all others via Claude Code. Higher is better unless noted. Headline: mean run score per Eq. (4), out of 100 (Table 3).

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench-LILT — overall pass rate
benchmarks.description: Terminal-Bench-LILT (arXiv 2608.28641, LILT Inc.): 300 terminal-based coding tasks in 10 languages (ar, cs, de, es, hi, ja, ko, sr, tr, zh; 30 each) targeting non-English-specific issues (internationalization, encoding, text normalization, cultural conventions), authored by native-speaker programmers in Harbor format; 3 difficulty tiers (133 easy / 86 medium / 81 hard). Terminus-2 harness, provider-default thinking, 5 trials per task-model pair; pass rate = share of trials passing. Higher is better. Aggregate pass rate over all 300 tasks x 5 trials (Figure 5).

benchmarks.name: PatchBench — Solved rate (Codex)
benchmarks.description: PatchBench (arXiv 2609.04075, Univ. of Maryland): 213 C/C++ repository-level vulnerability-patching tasks from 32 GitHub projects / 16 CWEs, built by vulnerability transplant + code mutation so ground-truth fixes lie outside the crash stack (mitigating patch memorization and stack-trace-only fixes). Agent gets the repo, PoC, sanitizer report and build commands in Docker; $5 budget per task, medium reasoning effort, no web access. Solved = patch passes both security validation (new PoCs / fuzzing) and semantic validation; PoC Pass = original PoC no longer crashes (inflates solve rate 1.83x). Higher is better. Scaffold: Codex.

benchmarks.name: SoftVTBench Object-Soft TSR (VO-C ID)
benchmarks.description: SoftVTBench (Tuojing Intelligence / Tsinghua, arXiv:2608.18701): visuo-tactile deformable-object manipulation benchmark (4,000 demos, 50+ assets, FEM ground truth). benchmarks.name: K-Bench overall score (0-10)

benchmarks.name: K-Bench majority-success rate

benchmarks.name: EarthVerse Core

benchmarks.name: BixBench3 average score

benchmarks.name: HW-design MCP tool-calling ECC (best ReAct config)

benchmarks.name: TruthInsightBench mean score

benchmarks.name: AgentIdeaBench Active weighted total
